title: VDW-GNNs: Vector diffusion wavelets for geometric graph neural networks
claim: Local frames built from neighborhood structure on a sampled manifold can be aligned across nodes by an orthogonal transformation.
layout: Manifold on top, two zoomed insets below, arrow with equation between them
description: A gray curved manifold surface fills the top of the figure, carrying black points joined by dashed k-NN graph edges. Two green-filled nodes have solid green lines to the neighbors used for local PCA. Blue arrows at each green node show the local coordinate frame. Red boxes mark these two nodes. Red lines connect each box to a larger inset below. Each inset shows a translucent 3D cube with blue axis arrows. The cubes are rotated differently and are labeled U_i on the left and U_j on the right. A curved black arrow runs from the right inset to the left inset. The equation O_{i,j} = U_i U_j^T sits above the arrow. The eye goes first to the red boxes and the blue frames, then to the equation.
caption: An example point cloud of data lying on a continuous manifold. Dashed lines: edges of a k-NN graph. Solid green lines: neighbor edges used to generate the local PCA for each node. Blue arrows: local coordinate systems/frames Ui and Uj induced by the local graph structure. Oi,j is the rotation that transforms Uj to Ui.
abstract: We introduce vector diffusion wavelets (VDWs), a novel family of wavelets inspired by the vector diffusion maps algorithm that was introduced to analyze data lying in the tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold. We show that these wavelets may be effectively incorporated into a family of geometric graph neural networks, which we refer to as VDW-GNNs. We demonstrate that such networks are effective on synthetic point cloud data, as well as on real-world data derived from wind field and neural activity measurements. Theoretically, we prove that these new wavelets have desirable frame theoretic properties, similar to traditional diffusion wavelets. Additionally, we prove that these wavelets have useful symmetries with respect to rotations and translations.
